wga:zearly/1/4mosaics/2ravenna/1galla/2l.summary: In a rocky green landscape beneath a starry blue vault, the young Christ sits among six sheep, reaching across to touch one that turns toward him. He wears a golden tunic with a purple mantle and a golden halo, and holds a tall golden cross instead of a shepherd's crook. The image fuses the gentle shepherd of the Gospel with the majesty of a ruler, one of the most beloved mosaics of the 5th century.
facts: The lunette is set over the north entrance of the building, built between 425 and 450 as a chapel adjoining the church of Santa Croce in Ravenna.
Despite its name, the empress Galla Placidia was not buried here; she died in Rome in 450, and the tradition of her burial in Ravenna dates from the 13th century.
The figure of a shepherd carrying a sheep was adopted from ancient art into Christian funerary art from the late 3rd century; here the shepherd is in imperial purple and gold.
